Coco Gauff ensured the watching American public had something to cheer at the US Open as she progressed to the fourth round on a day when Taylor Fritz, Amanda Anisimova and Madison Keys suffered shock defeats. Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16. The 22-year-old will next face the winner of compatriot Iva Jovic vs the Philippines's Alexandra Eala for a quarter-final spot. "I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said. messages.text: Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Carty falls through ropes in round one

metadata.summary: Dave Allen's heavyweight clash with Thomas Carty at Croke Park ended in a bizarre no contest after the Irish favourite fell out of the ring during the first round.
metadata.content: David Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Thomas Carty falls through ropes in round one on Katie Taylor undercard | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content David Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Thomas Carty falls through ropes in round one on Katie Taylor undercard Chief support bout for Katie Taylor's farewell fight was over in 82 seconds as Irish favourite, who was expected to win, tumbles through the ropes and is unable to continue; crowd jeered as incident was shown on Croke Park screens Saturday 5 September 2026 21:55, UK Image: Thomas Carty falls through the ropes during the first round of his fight with David Allen Dave Allen's heavyweight clash with Thomas Carty at Croke Park ended in a bizarre no contest after the Irish favourite fell out of the ring during the first round. The chief support for Katie Taylor's final fight before retirement was over after just 82 seconds with Carty - seeking the biggest win of his 12-bout career - unable to continue. Allen caught Carty on the back of the head with a clubbing right hand and the Dublin southpaw tumbled through the ropes as much through momentum as the shot itself and onto the floor, where he was laid on his back. messages.text: Taylor dominates Pili in final fight of career at Croke Park

metadata.summary: Katie Taylor bid an emotional farewell to boxing as the Irish icon dominated Flora Pili in the final fight of her storied career at a packed out Croke Park on Saturday.
metadata.content: Katie Taylor wins final fight of boxing career after beating Flora Pili on emotional night at Dublin's Croke Park | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Katie Taylor wins final fight of boxing career after beating Flora Pili on emotional night at Dublin's Croke Park Katie Taylor beats Flora Pili in the final fight of her boxing career, becoming an undisputed world champion for the third time; the judges score it 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 as Taylor headlines first boxing event at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972. Cam Hogwood NFL Journalist @ch_skysports Saturday 5 September 2026 23:23, UK Image: Katie Taylor celebrates the final win of her career Katie Taylor bid an emotional farewell to boxing as the Irish icon dominated Flora Pili in the final fight of her storied career at a packed out Croke Park on Saturday. The 40-year-old stormed to a unanimous decision victory to clinch the vacant WBC super-lightweight belt and bow out as a three-time undisputed world champion with 84,000 fans in attendance at Dublin's historic sporting home. Taylor, an Olympic champion and two-weight undisputed champion, hangs up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest female boxer in history and a game-changing pioneer for women's sport. It marked the first boxing event to be held at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al "Blue" Lewis on July 19, 1972. messages.text: 'Out in the middle of nowhere' - Hamilton rues Ferrari's handling of qualifying

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton felt Ferrari’s execution of the final stage of Italian Grand Prix qualifying had been "pretty bad" after the home team’s hopes of being able to challenge for pole position on Saturday fell flat.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says team's execution of Italian GP qualifying could have been better after 'very tough' session | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says team's execution of Italian GP qualifying could have been better after 'very tough' session Lewis Hamilton almost dropped out in Q2 before going on to finish fifth fastest in Q3, which became fourth on the grid behind team-mate Charles Leclerc; watch the Italian Grand Prix live on Sunday at 2pm on Sky Sports F1, with build-up from 12.30pm Saturday 5 September 2026 19:18, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc reflect on Ferrari's frustrating lack of pace during qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza. Lewis Hamilton felt Ferrari’s execution of the final stage of Italian Grand Prix qualifying had been "pretty bad" after the home team’s hopes of being able to challenge for pole position on Saturday fell flat. Ferrari had been tipped to contend for pole at their home Monza race but never truly appeared in the hunt at any stage of the knockout sessions with the Scuderia eventually outpaced in Q3 by three Mercedes-powered cars - including Alpine surprise polesitter Pierre Gasly. Oscar Piastri's later three-place grid penalty means Charles Leclerc and Hamilton will still both start on the second row in third and fourth places respectively.
